title: Chapter 1: Today is a Good Day to Throw My Life Away 4
content: "You were in my class, weren't you?"
I'm so glad... truly glad.
I had been remembered by Erika Solnzali. Living up to this moment felt worthwhile; my life wasn't in vain.
Erika Solnzali placed her right hand against her temple, as if digging deeper into her memories.
"Yes... that's right, you were among the crowd that only watched from a distance."
In that instant, I became acutely aware of my face turning bright red.
She had seen through me, Erika Solnzali herself. She had noticed the inappropriate affection I harbored for her. I wanted to commend myself for not screaming out in embarrassment.
I instinctively averted my gaze.
"Why are you suddenly looking away?"
Erika Solnzali asked, her expression one of curiosity.
Did she truly understand what she had just said?
What kind of face was I supposed to make when the one who had been "watching" me was now telling me that she had been "watched"?
"What are you so embarrassed about? It's not like the 'real person' is here."
Perhaps my appearance was too pitiful, prompting Erika Solnzali to make a joke to lighten the mood. How kind; I liked her.
The affection I felt for her outweighed my embarrassment, and my heart began to calm.
When I faced her again, I caught a glimpse of her exasperated expression.
Erika Solnzali hesitated for just a moment.
"Could it be that you are my nominal husband?"
Oh, God.

The moment those words left Erika Solnzali's lips, I was enveloped in a sensation akin to bliss and omnipotence, only to feel my blood run cold in an instant. For her, it might have been a trivial confirmation. But for me, it was anything but.
To affirm those words, even if they were merely a role in a farcical play, required seriousness and resolve. I became aware that my face had stiffened slightly.
Seeing this, Erika Solnzali raised her eyebrows just a bit.
"Yes, I am the man who will become your husband."
I could feel sweat trickling down my back, but I didn't think of it as unpleasant sweat.
After gazing intently at my face, Erika Solnzali broke into a smile that was almost a wry grin.
"You can make such a noble face, can't you?"
What kind of face did she think that was? Erika Solnzali looked at me with a nostalgic expression.
"If I had known you could make such a face, I would have introduced you to someone."
Who exactly was she talking about introducing me to?
If she said "noble," it must have been someone important, right? Not that I was particularly interested.
"So, what is your purpose here? I can make some guesses, but..."
I felt a flutter in my chest as she tilted her head, resting her hand on her cheek.
"That means I don't understand why you are here."
Hmm? What was my purpose? I pondered for a moment, struggling to figure out how to respond.

I couldn't just say, "I was happy to hear that I could become your husband, even if nominally," could I? Even I understood that much. Sure, I had no experience with women, having come from a poor viscount family, and I was aware that I wasn't very accustomed to them, but I still understood.
How cringeworthy that response would be.
But what was I supposed to say?
How do charming men respond in situations like this?
She was aware of my feelings, having seen me looking at her, and now she was asking why I was here. How was I supposed to answer that?
Oh no, Erika Solnzali was waiting for my response. I couldn't remain silent.
I somehow managed to muster the words, hoping I wouldn't be called cringeworthy.
"I... I just wish to be by your side, even if just a little."
Was that answer acceptable? I felt a different kind of unpleasant sweat trickling down due to my nerves.
"Honestly..."
Erika Solnzali opened her mouth.
"Despite the way you say it, you choose such roundabout options."
She spoke as if looking at something troublesome, but there was no hint of disdain or disgust in her voice, just a tone that seemed to care for someone clumsy.
At least it seemed I wasn't thought of as cringeworthy.
And what did she mean by "roundabout"? She was right in front of me.
"So, how long will you stay with me?"
"Huh? How long?"
When I asked back, she responded with a slightly exasperated tone, yet still with the demeanor of someone trying to guide a wayward younger sibling.
"The period during which you will stay with me. I assume you negotiated that with my father."
Negotiate with the Prime Minister? What was she talking about? Perhaps because Erika Solnzali was so intelligent, she had a tendency to jump ahead in conversations since our academy days.
In other words, I couldn't keep up with her quick thinking, and I began to think.
I didn't remember negotiating with the Prime Minister, but I had indeed met and spoken with him.
The content was likely something along the lines of "Please take care of my daughter." But what did she mean by "period"? Wait, was it the period during which I would stay with her?
Oh, I see... what a misunderstanding I had.
She had no obligation to humor this farce.
Erika Solnzali could live perfectly well on her own.
So, the "period" referred to the time she would humor this farce and allow me to stay by her side.
I felt embarrassed, as if she had seen through my shallow thinking that I could stay by her side simply by taking on the role in this farce.
It couldn't be that easy to remain by Erika Solnzali's side.
I gazed intently into her eyes. If I said I wanted to stay for a lifetime, would she accept it?
For some reason, Erika Solnzali flinched as she looked at me.
"One year. Would you allow me to stay by your side for one year?"
I awaited her response with the heart of a condemned man waiting for judgment.
"One year..."
Erika Solnzali murmured, looking troubled.
"That is quite a long period, isn't it?"
Oh no, I struggled to keep my disappointment from showing on my face.
"Your father is certainly being quite shrewd."
Huh? What did the Prime Minister have to do with this? She let out another one of her slightly too loud soliloquies.
"Given the current situation, it would be easy for 'him' to decide who to introduce 'her' to for about a year, but still... one year is..."
The important person she was trying to introduce was a woman? Who could it be?
I felt a strange guilt for interrupting her soliloquy, but I did so anyway.
"No, it's not that the Prime Minister said anything."
Erika Solnzali looked at me with a puzzled expression.
"Is that so?"
I nodded in response to her question.
"Then, did you propose the one-year period?"
I had just said that! I thought, but I nodded anyway.
"How should I put it? I don't dislike the determination to go to any lengths for your purpose, but..."
If she showed such determination, I was sure her father would do everything in his power to keep that promise.
It was hard to tell if she was speaking to herself or making a judgment with her murmurs.
"Still, you didn't have to stick with me so faithfully. You could have just accepted the title of nominal husband and vanished within the kingdom."
But that wouldn't allow me to stay by her side, which would defeat the purpose, I thought, as her words reminded me.
"Speaking of which, the Prime Minister said something similar, of course, I declined."
Our conversation was starting to feel more like a clash of soliloquies, but Erika Solnzali expressed slight surprise.
Then, for some reason, she looked at my face intently and straightened her posture.
By the way, her posture had been beautiful all along.
"Yes... that option was presented. Yet, you chose to stay with me."
Her gaze was beautiful as she looked at me.
Her abundant magic power enveloped her, shimmering beautifully in response to her delicate movements.
The words that flowed from her lips were imbued with emotion that struck deep within my chest.
"To stay by your side, even for just a little, I would throw away a year."
Was that feeling sincerity?
"I may have underestimated your resolve. I apologize. And I don't dislike that resolve."
She smiled.
"Shin Longdagger, I have taken a liking to you."
[img]https://i.imgur.com/rxzS9Au.jpeg
To be liked by Erika Solnzali. Just that fact alone made me feel faint.
At the edge of my fading consciousness, I thought I heard her whisper, "I wish someone would think of me like this," but I couldn't comprehend what she was saying.
I was too happy.
Two hours had passed since Erika Solnzali revived and told me she liked me, and I almost fainted.

During that time, she had suddenly recalled the root cause of this ridiculous situation and nearly turned into a curse-spewing machine. I also recalled the moments when she had said she liked me and felt faint again.
Merseja informed us from the driver's seat that we were about to finish our first day's journey.
"Sir, I can see the town where we'll be staying tonight."
I wasn't particularly interested, but since he had taken the time to speak, I opened the window on the side that hadn't been blown away and looked ahead.
I could see a small town in the grassland. I think its name was Sudabardo.
I had memories of coming here several times for adventurer work, but it hadn't left much of an impression.
Because of that, my interest shifted elsewhere.
"By the way, Merseja."
"What's up, sir?"
Merseja replied with a relaxed tone that made me question his suitability as a guard.
"There really weren't any additional attacks, were there? Your assessment was spot on, as expected."
Merseja let out a strange chuckle and said proudly.
"There’s no organization that can send out assassins of that level so casually. For them, losing their prized assets is no small matter."
And easily too, I thought internally, glancing at the face of the one who had easily taken them down.
The subject of our discussion seemed oblivious, enjoying the scenery outside the window.
"Why do you look like you have nothing to do with it, sir?"
Merseja complained in exasperation. While it was fine to complain, he should focus on driving.

"Well... even if there had been plans for additional attacks, we are unscathed and on guard. They would likely want to regroup and, if possible, leave their territory quickly enough to not offend the client."
While I tried not to let my guard down, I found myself agreeing with Merseja.

Adventurers are human too; they can fall from grace for various reasons. However, the higher the rank, the rarer that becomes. Even if they fall from grace a bit, if they have the skills of a high-ranking adventurer, they will have many opportunities. It's simply rare for someone to fall to the point of being picked up by a criminal organization.

The attackers certainly had skills comparable to high-ranking adventurers. Whether they were former adventurers or unique individuals who had gained such strength in the wild, that point remained unchanged.
Indeed, as Merseja said, that kind of strength would be precious to an organization.
If they were to lose that, it would be a significant blow.
However, I thought.
The enemy was made up of people who could transform humans into members of the Demon Race through unknown means.
It would be overly optimistic to think of them as an organization that would think rationally.
Perhaps my expression revealed my thoughts, as Merseja smiled wryly.
"At least in the town, we should be safe."
If humans were to turn into members of the Demon Race in the town, it would cause a huge uproar.
Saying that, Merseja laughed.
The town of Sudabardo was equipped with what is known as water-generating magic tools and barrier devices.

In other words, they created all the water needed for drinking and daily life using water-generating magic tools, and instead of surrounding the town with walls to protect it from monsters and external enemies, they used barrier devices to create a massive barrier to safeguard the town.
Of course, both methods required an enormous amount of magic power.
It was far from realistic to continuously supply such magic power using magic stones.
Therefore, Sudabardo adopted the method that other similar towns had employed.
In other words──.
I felt a slight chill, as if my magic power was being drawn from me.
Merseja and the horses pulling the carriage seemed to feel the same chill, shivering slightly.
The only one who showed no reaction was Erika Solnzali.
After completing the necessary procedures to enter the town and stepping into the barrier, I felt a slight drain of magic power.
The town's residents gradually absorbed magic power to create water and form the barrier.
That was the method adopted by towns like Sudabardo.
To my eyes, which could see magic power, I could see streams of magic power rising from all over the town.
Countless streams of magic power; some might even call it beautiful.
But I couldn't help but follow just one stream with my eyes.
The golden stream of Erika Solnzali's magic power.
